title: Current Gamblers on Legal Online Gambling Sites Operated by Singapore Pools and Singapore Turf Club
what_it_is: Current Gamblers on Legal Online Gambling Sites Operated by Singapore Pools and Singapore Turf Club

sections.label: Remote betting account holders
sections.summary: Over 95% of new telephone betting account holders had placed bets in the preceding 12 months, and turnover growth stayed in line with earlier years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Among those who had previously not held telephone betting accounts, over 95% of them indicated that they had placed bets with the operators in the preceding 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In short, the large majority do not appear to be first-time gamblers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: It is not possible to ascertain whether these remote account holders have simply switched from other platforms, including illegal ones, or have increased their total gambling.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: That said, there has not been evidence of a surge in the sum of bets placed with Singapore Pools and Singapore Turf Club since the commencement of remote services in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In 2017, Singapore Pools and Singapore Turf Club's turnover grew by 2.6%, in line with the average annual growth of 2.4% between financial year (FY) 2012 and FY2015.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: On the other hand, according to gambling consultancy firm H2GC, the local underground remote gambling market grew only by 0.3% in 2017, lower than the average annual growth rate of 3.1% between 2012 and 2016.
